nodes.name: A lead email arrives
nodes.notes:
Watches ONLY mail sent to the +leads address, so the rest of the inbox is never read.

Simplify is OFF on purpose: the simplified response carries only Gmail's ~200-character snippet, which cuts the email off mid-sentence and hides the signature. The facts we need - company, size, frequency, who is actually writing - are usually below that line.

Gmail is polled about once a minute, so email leads are not instant. Form and webhook leads are.

nodes.name: Pull the lead out of the email

options.systemPromptTemplate:
You read an email sent to a commercial cleaning company and pull out the facts about the enquiry.

Only record what the email actually says. If something is not stated, leave it empty or zero - never guess a size, a city or a company. A wrong fact here becomes a wrong score, and then a wrong decision.

nodes.notes: An email is prose, not a form: the facts have to be read out of it. If this fails, the lead still continues - the pipeline treats it as unscored rather than losing it.

nodes.name: Hand it to the pipeline
nodes.notes: Waits here, unlike the other sources: the email must not be marked as read until the lead is safely through the pipeline.

nodes.name: Mark the email as read
nodes.notes: Stops the same email becoming a lead every minute. It runs only after the pipeline has finished. A failed lead is not retried - the trigger never re-reads a message it has seen - it goes to the Quarantine tab and Telegram instead.
